  "concordance_definition": "The study defines concordance as the relationship between published data and in-house data, categorizing outcomes as 'completely in line', 'main set was reproducible', 'some results were reproducible', or 'data showed inconsistencies that led to project termination'.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Data set is rather small and its statistical significance can be questioned.",
    "Own experimental results might also be irreproducible in other laboratories.",
    "The study does not report fraud, but a lack of reproducibility."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "The authors are employees of Bayer Healthcare.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "Success rates for new development projects in Phase II trials have fallen from 28% to 18%.",
    "23 scientists provided input for the analysis.",
    "Data were collected from 67 projects.",
    "47 projects were from the field of oncology.",
    "Only in ~20-25% of projects were published data completely in line with in-house findings.",
    "In almost two-thirds of projects, there were inconsistencies between published and in-house data.",
    "Intra- and interscreen reproducibility of two genome-scale small interfering RNA screens ranged from 32-99%.",
    "An unspoken rule among early-stage venture capital firms states that 'at least 50% of published studies... can’t be repeated with the same conclusions by an industrial lab'."
  ]
